description: With the excitement of Georgia deer hunting season, archery and firearm safety can get lax, and that can mean danger for children.
shortAnswer: Many unintentional gunshot wounds and deaths occur in or nearby the home of family friends or relatives. When a child is injured by a weapon and that injury could have been prevented by the owner of the weapon or owner of the premises where the injury occurred, a careful investigation by an attorney is advisable.

faq.q: When can the family of a child injured or killed by a gunshot or arrow seek legal help?
faq.a: ANYTIME a child is injured legal relief may be available. Anyone who has been through one of the Georgia hunter education courses has been trained how to protect children from gunshot injuries, and that training creates legal duties to any children that are in the hunter's home or vehicle or other premise.

faq.q: Is a gun owner liable if a child finds a gun and ammunition stored together?
faq.a: Ammunition should be stored AWAY from the weapons themselves. Violation of these safety rules can create a situation where a child finds a gun and ammunition together and loads and fires the weapon. A firearm owner that violates these rules with injury or death resulting is going to face legal liability.

faq.q: Are hunters responsible for what their shot hits beyond the target?
faq.a: Hunters and weapon owners are legally responsible for what comes out of their weapons. If a shooter cannot see what lies beyond the target they have a duty to not take the shot.

faq.q: Can a family seek punitive damages if a hunter was drinking or using drugs?
faq.a: Injuries that result from hunting and handling firearms after consuming alcohol or drugs are inexcusable and form the basis for a punitive damages claim against the offender.
